title: The second postcard
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Wood answers. The second of the ten. Written in the Datsun in Lot C with the dog's head on the wheel. Mailed from the college. The strip shows the slot. Eight — no. Seven left.

panels.composition: The Datsun in Lot C. WOOD writing a postcard on the wheel. BARNABY's head resting on the wheel's top, in the way.

image.prompt: a young man writing a postcard against a car's steering wheel while a small dog rests its head on top of the wheel, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The card's front: the bay, blue. His thumb over the writing side. The strip's rule.

image.prompt: close on a faded postcard of a bay held with a thumb covering its back, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The college's mail slot in the lobby wall. The card going in.

image.prompt: close on a postcard being slipped into a brass mail slot in a college lobby wall, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The drawer at home that night: seven. He counts twice. The unsent one is in the box; it doesn't count, and it does.

image.prompt: close on a desk drawer with seven postcards being counted by a young man's hand, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Seven in the drawer, one in the box, two mailed. The strip counts twice.
